  Urgency Ordinance  No. 1095 -  Community Development Director Scherer reported on the Urgency Ordinance
  Extension of Moratorium  on  No. 1095-  Extension of Moratorium  on  Short Term Rentals.  He stated that at

  Short Term Rentals  the March 2, 2020 Council meeting, the City Council adopted Urgency
  Ordinance No. 1092, an extension of the moratorium on short- term ( less than
  30 days) rentals due to concerns raised by residents. The City Council
  approved an extension six months ( September 2, 2020) with the expectation of
  holding a study session with the short- term rental hosts to craft an ordinance to
  be reviewed by the Council  before the  moratorium  expired.  Due to COVID- 19

  however, this study session has yet to be held. Staff is requesting that the
  moratorium be extended through August 17, 2021, with expectations of
  drafting an ordinance sooner. The additional time is needed in order to
  appropriately host the study session and prepare a draft ordinance to
  permanently regulate this use.

  The City Council agreed with the extension of the moratorium and that staff
  within a month' s time would survey the Airbnb hosts on their concerns.

  It was moved by Carder, seconded by Crosby, and unanimously carried to
  approve Urgency Ordinance No. 1095 extending the moratorium of short- term
  less than 30 days) rentals for a period not to extend past August 17, 2021.

re:  8- 17- 20 City Council meeting - agenda item Sh ( exchange  of
  Prop. A funds)
Comments to share  with  the City Council in advance  of the  City Council meeting and include in the meeting
record:

Once again  we  see  La Verne exchanging unused Proposition A transportation funds  at a significant  discount in
order  to transfer  money to general  fund use. In this case the $ 280, 000 exchange  with  the City of Hawaiian

Gardens at seventy- five cents  on  the dollar equals  a  loss of$ 70, 000 for La Verne. Cumulatively transfers like
this  add
  up to  hundreds of thousands  of  dollars lost, and  millions  in diverted transportation funding.

In the zniddle  of a pandemic  that' s put  unprecedented  strain  on  the general  fund it doesn' t make sense to question
this year' s exchange -  short term
  solvency needs to be prioritized. But taking a long- range  view  it should be
recognized  that this practice perpetuates neglect of public transportation issues.

I hese exchanges  areroutinely approved as consent calendar items every year without any review of the
effectiveness  of the City' s Prop. A spending, nor any consideration of how these funds might be better put to use

benefiting  those  who  are  dependent. Budget documents indicate that the City has simply found easy
  transit-

ways  to disperse  some
  Prop. A money, leaving unspent funds that can be traded for general fund money to be
spent  elsewhere.

Finding effective  ways  to meet the transportation  needs  of all  can  be a challenge  with  no  simple  solutions,  but

doing so can help ensure a healthy community  where  everyone  shares
  quality  the sort  of  of  life that strengthens

community  spirit.  I hope the Council and the new Active Transportation Committee will take a serious look at
the long- neglected state of public transportation in La Verne.

Brian Bennett
La Verne

for  new  community  spaces  and  reinvigorated  downtowns.  Let' s transform this space from asphalt
reserved for empty cars, to a healthy, more useful space for the community to come together and
thrive!
